topic: Claude Sonnet 5.5: faster agent work at lower per-task cost
caption:
Claude Sonnet 5.5 is a good reminder that model upgrades are not just about benchmark scores.

Anthropic reports 30%+ faster output generation than Sonnet 5 and up to 30% lower cost per task for most work. The interesting detail? Its per-token API prices are unchanged. The efficiency gain comes from how much work the model gets done with fewer tokens and faster execution.

For developers building AI agents, that changes the economics of everyday workflows.

I'd evaluate Sonnet 5.5 for targeted code changes, repeated tool calls, document generation, and other well-scoped tasks. For long-running, ambiguous decisions, I'd still route work to a model better suited to sustained judgment.

Before migrating, check your model ID, thinking settings, and tool-choice behavior. Then benchmark your own workload rather than assuming published results will translate directly.

The real question isn't 'Which model is smartest?' It's 'Which model is reliable enough for this task at the right cost?'

Source: Anthropic announcement and Claude Platform Docs
